text:
ConocoPhillips ticked up slightly today, gaining less than 0.3%, as oil prices held relatively steady with U.S. crude at $82.24 per barrel. The modest move comes after the stock fell sharply on November 23rd (down to $132.19), suggesting today's small gain represents some modest recovery rather than fresh momentum. The recovery aligns with stabilization in crude prices and continued positioning in energy stocks among analysts looking for dividend-paying plays.

The broader backdrop remains mixed for oil majors. While energy companies could benefit from growing AI infrastructure demand that may push power consumption and energy needs higher across Latin America and globally, the collapse of climate negotiations at COP31 — which failed to include any language on fossil fuels — removes near-term regulatory uncertainty but also reflects mounting political headwinds the sector faces. This tension between structural demand tailwinds and policy resistance has likely kept investors cautious, explaining why the stock is still down 2% over two weeks despite holding up today.
